h1:
Chiang Rai with the Family
3 Days, 2 Nights with Kids
intro: Taking kids to Chiang Rai is easier than you'd think — you just have to plan the order well so you're not stacking temples back-to-back until the kids melt down. This plan alternates pretty temples, a tea farm where they can run around, and a flower park with animals to look at. We've spread it over 3 days and 2 nights, with no more than about an hour and a half of driving per day, leaving plenty of time for the kids to rest and eat at an easy pace.

blocks.html: Chiang Rai is fun with kids because a lot of the sights are outdoors with wide-open space, so the kids can run around and see animals instead of just walking past Buddha images. But a few of them do need some planning around opening hours and dress code. So we mapped out a route that doesn't double back — less driving, more sightseeing.

items: Day 1 — In and around the city: the White Temple (Wat Rong Khun) + Wat Huay Pla Kang (with a lift up the giant statue), so the kids don't have to walk far
Day 2 — North side: Singha Park — flower gardens, tea fields, and an animal farm, with a tram ride all day. The kids' favorite
Day 3 — Mae Chan district: Choui Fong tea farm — sip tea and grab a green tea cake before heading home

blocks.title: Before You Set Off
blocks.html: Chiang Rai is cool from November to February, which is the best time to bring kids — but the midday sun is strong, so pack hats, sunscreen, and drinking water. Most of the sights are outdoors, so sneakers beat sandals.

blocks.text: Day 1 — City Temples, Easy Walking for Kids

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: White Temple + Wat Huay Pla Kang

items.activity: Leave your in-town hotel for the White Temple (Wat Rong Khun), about 13 km from the city center — a 20-minute drive
items.note: Go early, before the tour buses arrive — fewer people and easier photos

items.activity: Walk the White Temple, an all-white temple with fine sculpture work, plus a bridge to cross and an art hall for the kids to wander through
items.note: Free for Thai nationals; 200 THB for foreigners, including the art hall · Open Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00, Sat–Sun until 17:30 · Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered; free sarongs are available to borrow

items.activity: Stop for lunch at a northern-Thai restaurant near the temple — try khao soi or nam ngiao
items.note: Northern food isn't heavily spiced, so kids can usually handle it; if you're worried about heat, ask for the chilies on the side

items.activity: Head to Wat Huay Pla Kang to see the giant 69-meter Guanyin statue
items.note: There's a lift up to floors 22–23 for views over Chiang Rai · Lift is 20 THB for Thais, 40 THB for foreigners · Temple open 07:00–21:00, lift until 18:00

items.activity: Head back into town, rest at the hotel and let the kids nap, then go out to the Chiang Rai Clock Tower in the evening
items.note: The Clock Tower has a light show every hour, with rounds at 19:00 / 20:00 / 21:00 — kids love it · The night market is an easy walk nearby

blocks.title: Tips for Visiting Temples with Kids
blocks.html: The White Temple and Wat Huay Pla Kang are in different parts of town, but neither involves much walking and both have parking close by. If your kids are very young, bring a stroller — the paths at the White Temple are smooth enough to push one.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Singha Park, a Full Day Kids Won't Tire Of

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Singha Park — Flower Gardens + Animal Farm

items.activity: Leave the city for Singha Park, about 12 km away — a 20-minute drive
items.note: An agricultural park spanning over 8,000 rai. Free entry, open daily 08:30–17:00 · Some activities inside cost extra

items.activity: Buy farm-tour tickets and ride the tram around the tea fields, flower gardens, and animal farm
items.note: Tram is 150 THB for adults, 50 THB for kids · Much easier than walking it yourself, and great for families

items.activity: Get off at the animal farm so the kids can see and feed giraffes, zebras, Watusi cattle, and capybaras
items.note: Animal feed is sold separately by the bag · The giraffe-feeding spot is a big hit, but keep an eye on little ones in case the animals startle them

items.activity: Lunch in the park — there are restaurants and a café where you can sit with a view over the tea fields
items.note: There's a kids' menu and snacks; prices are what you'd expect at a tourist resort, so budget a bit extra

items.activity: Walk the flower gardens for photos — in the cool season lots of flowers are in bloom, including fields of yellow blossoms
items.note: If you're after something more adventurous, there's a zipline for adults and older kids, with a separate fee

items.activity: Head back into town to relax, then find dinner at a market in the city
items.note: Kids who've played all day usually crash early, so keep tonight's dinner light

blocks.text: Day 3 — Choui Fong Tea Farm, Tea Before Heading Home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Choui Fong Tea Farm, Mae Chan District

items.activity: Check out and leave the city for Choui Fong tea farm in Mae Chan district, about 40 km away — a 1-hour drive
items.note: The last stretch up the hill is winding, so bring motion-sickness medicine if your kids are prone to it

items.activity: Walk the green terraced tea fields and take photos of the mountain views
items.note: Free entry, open daily 08:30–17:30 · The paths are a bit hilly, so hold little ones' hands

items.activity: Head into the Choui Fong café for green tea, green tea crepe cake, and green tea soft-serve
items.note: There's seating both indoors and outdoors with tea-field views · Around 100–250 THB per person · Kids love the soft-serve

items.activity: Lunch around Mae Chan, then drive home or continue to Chiang Rai airport
items.note: Choui Fong to Mae Fah Luang Airport is about 30–40 minutes, so leave enough time

blocks.html: If your kids are very young, or if it rains, there are some backup kid-friendly spots in town. Most are cafés with indoor play areas where the kids can burn off energy without being out in the sun.

items.name: Vanasuwan Farm
items.blurb: A farm café in the Chang Phuek area in town, with alpacas and other cute animals for the kids to see and feed — and you can sit down for a coffee too.

items.name: Potta World Cafe & Playground
items.blurb: An indoor amusement spot in the Tha Sai area with a ball pit, trampolines, and a coloring corner. Open daily 08:00–20:00 — good for rainy days.

items.name: Akha Farmville
items.blurb: A sheep farm up on Doi Chang in Mae Suai district — feed the sheep and walk around taking in the mountain views. Good if you're heading out to Doi Chang.

blocks.title: Where to Stay with the Family
blocks.html: With kids, we'd stay in the city of Chiang Rai, near the Clock Tower and night market where food is easy to find. You can drive to the White Temple, Singha Park, and Wat Huay Pla Kang in about 20 minutes. Pick a hotel with a kids' pool to cool off in the evening.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Chiang Rai with kids?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just about right — one day for the city temples, a full day at Singha Park, and Choui Fong tea farm before you head home. If you're short on time, you can cut it to 2 days and 1 night by combining the White Temple and Singha Park into one day.

faq.q: Which Chiang Rai sight do kids like best?
faq.a: Singha Park is usually the kids' favorite — you ride the tram around the tea fields and get to feed giraffes, zebras, and capybaras, with plenty of open space to run around. The tram is 150 THB for adults and 50 THB for kids.

faq.q: What do you need to bring to take young kids into the White Temple?
faq.a: Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered; the temple lends out sarongs for free. The paths are fairly smooth, so you can push a stroller. Thai nationals enter free. It's best to go in the morning before it gets crowded and the sun gets strong.

faq.q: Is the driving between sights long?
faq.a: Not in this plan. The White Temple and Singha Park are about 12–13 km from the city, a 20-minute drive. Choui Fong tea farm is the farthest at about 40 km, an hour's drive — the last stretch up the hill is winding, so bring motion-sickness medicine if your kids are prone to it.

faq.q: When is the best time to bring kids to Chiang Rai?
faq.a: November to February is best — cool, comfortable weather, and lots of flowers in bloom at Singha Park. Most of the sights are outdoors, so in the hot and rainy seasons it's worth lining up some indoor backups.
